site.name: Santorini (Thera) and its Bronze Age eruption

centre.how: Centroid of Nea Kameni (OpenStreetMap coastline), near the middle of the flooded caldera

claimed.line: The Bronze Age eruption of Thera is the real event behind Plato's story of an island that sank in a day and night.
claimed.evidence: The explosion, the Atlanticists argue, was “remembered” in a mixed-up way, until Plato brought it back to consciousness in his myth.

found.line: The eruption was real and buried Akrotiri, but dates 8,000 years after Plato's. Nothing ties it to his text.
found.who: Friedrich and others; Pearson and others
found.evidence: Calibrated results and growth increment counts indicate increased probabilities for a mid-16th century BCE date for the eruption

features.label: Nea Kameni (after 1600 BCE)
features.what: A lava island built inside the caldera after the Bronze Age eruption. It did not exist in 1600 BCE.

position.detail: OpenStreetMap natural=coastline way, simplified to about 5 m

features.evidence: Repeated effusive eruptions since the LBA eruption have built up the Kameni Volcano within the resulting caldera
features.notes: Karatson 2018 calls both Kameni islands post-Minoan. Strabo described an eruption in 197 BC (Druitt and others 1999, excerpt only).

position.detail: OSM node 1842740533 place=town name=Φηρά

features.evidence: place=town; name=Φηρά; name:en=Fira

features.label: Kolumbo submarine volcano
features.what: A submarine volcano about 8 km north-east of Santorini; its crater floor is about 505 m below the sea. It last erupted in 1650 CE.

position.detail: Fig. 1a (PDF page 3): centre of the dark-blue crater; lon from the vector axis labels 25 15 to 25 35 E, lat from 36 20 to 36 30 N. Wikipedia gives 36.5167 N 25.4917 E, which is 1.1 km away

features.evidence: Kolumbo (Greek: Κολούμπο) is an active submarine volcano in the Aegean Sea in Greece
features.notes: Position from the Nature Communications map; IODP sites U1590 and U1593 say they are 5 km and 8 km north-west of the Kolumbo caldera, which fits this point better than the Wikipedia one.

features.label: Santorini as the seed of Atlantis
features.what: These authors read the Bronze Age eruption of Thera as the real event behind Plato's story of a sunken island.

position.detail: The proposal names the island, not a spot; the point is the middle of the caldera (centroid of Nea Kameni, OpenStreetMap)

features.evidence: The explosion, the Atlanticists argue, was “remembered” in a mixed-up way, until Plato brought it back to consciousness in his myth.
features.notes: Quote is from Moses Finley, a critic, describing the proposal. Marinatos 1939 (Antiquity 13) is about Minoan Crete; its abstract does not mention Atlantis. The Atlantis link is made by later writers.

features.label: Akrotiri, the buried Bronze Age town
features.what: Excavated town buried by the eruption. The mapped polygon is the protective roof over the dig.
features.result: A multi-storey town with frescoes was found under pumice and ash. It shows the eruption was real. It says nothing about Plato.

position.detail: OSM way 299988161 (building=roof, name=Ancient Akrotiri, wikidata Q421232). The roof covers the excavated part; the buried town extends beyond it

features.evidence: Because of the site being preserved in thick, volcanic debris, Marinatos noted that many of the buildings were preserved to a height of more than a single storey
features.notes: Footprint is the roof outline in OpenStreetMap, not an official plan; the Greek Ministry of Culture page could not be fetched. Wikipedia gives the centre as 36.35139 N 25.40361 E, inside this polygon.

features.label: Olive branch, Phira quarry (2006 dating)
features.what: An olive branch buried alive in the Minoan pumice was dated by radiocarbon to fix the year of the eruption.
features.result: The outer ring dated to 1627 to 1600 BCE (95.4%). Later work says olive rings may not be yearly, so this date is argued.

position.detail: Pearson and others 2023 place it "at Phira Quarry" on the caldera wall (Fig. 1b). The point is the centre of the nearest OpenStreetMap quarry polygon (way 377120199), 450 m from the dot on their schematic map

features.evidence: a sample retrieved from an olive tree (hereafter called the Santorini olive) buried under the > 60-m-thick Minoan pumice layer exposed in the caldera wall at Phira Quarry
features.notes: Friedrich 2006 (Science 312:548) says only "on Santorini"; I could not read its supplement. The quarry is identified from Pearson 2023. Date quote from Friedrich: "1627–1600 B.C. (2σ, 95% confidence)".

features.label: Olive shrub, Therasia (2023 dating)
features.what: A charred olive shrub under the pumice on Therasia was dated as a second test of the eruption date.
features.result: It is slightly younger than the Phira branch and favours a mid-16th century BCE eruption.

position.detail: "near the present day Monastery of Panaghia Koimisis, on the southern-most tip of the island of Therasia". Point is the south tip of the Therasia coast (OpenStreetMap). Their schematic Fig. 1b dot sits further north, about 1.6 km away

features.evidence: found during excavations near the present day Monastery of Panaghia Koimisis, on the southern-most tip of the island of Therasia
features.notes: The two position clues disagree (text says southern tip, schematic dot is mid-island). Treat as the Koimisis hill at the south end of Therasia.

features.label: Palaikastro, Crete: tsunami deposits
features.what: Fieldwork on the Minoan town and its beach cliffs found chaotic layers of ash, building stone and shells, read as a tsunami.
features.result: Run-up of at least 9 m, after the first ash fall. The date matches the eruption. About 155 km from the caldera.

position.detail: OSM way 35535089 (Roussolakkos, alt name "Paleokastro Minoan Town", wikidata Q3443476). The cliff sections were on the East Beach and Promontory a few hundred metres away

features.evidence: Field evidence suggests that tsunami waves at Palaikastro were at least 9 m high.
features.notes: Polygon is the mapped Minoan town, not the exact cliff sections. This feature is about 155 km from the caldera, so the scene needs a wide view or an inset.

features.label: NW strait study area (Nomikou 2016)
features.what: Area of the north-west gap in the caldera rim shown in detailed maps, from multibeam (2001, 2006, 2015) and seismic surveys.
features.result: The strait is a 3 km long, 1 km wide channel cut by the sea rushing in after the eruption.

position.detail: Fig. 1a (PDF page 3): orange box edges found by colour; lon and lat from the vector axis labels (25 15 to 25 35 E, 36 20 to 36 30 N)

features.evidence: Orange box outlines the area of the northwest strait
features.notes: The box marks the map area, not the outline of the ship survey. Multibeam data are available on request only.

features.label: Seismic line B-B′ along NW strait
features.what: Seismic reflection line along the axis of the north-west strait into the north basin.
features.result: Shows the caldera fill in layers 1 to 3 and a channel carved into lava, with no deep faults under the breach.

position.detail: Fig. 2a (PDF page 4): dashed line B-B′ taken from the vector drawing; lon and lat from the vector tick marks (25 20 to 25 23 E, 36 26 to 36 30 N)

features.evidence: Interpreted multi-channel reflection seismic profile along the axis of the NW strait.
features.notes: Methods: "Multi-channel seismic data were collected during RV POSEIDON cruise P338 in 2006 and during the 'ATLANTIS FOUND' project in 2015." The paper does not say which cruise shot this line.

features.label: Seismic line A-A′ across NW strait
features.what: Seismic reflection line across the north-west strait.
features.result: Shows a steep U-shaped channel with thin caldera-fill layers on its floor.

position.detail: Fig. 2a (PDF page 4): dashed line A-A′ from the vector drawing; ticks as for B-B′

features.evidence: Seismic profile perpendicular to the strait axis, showing caldera-fill stratigraphic units 1 and 2 of ref. 10.

features.label: Headwall of the NW strait
features.what: The curved scar at the north end of the channel where the sea cut into the caldera wall.
features.result: Read as a fossil "water chute": the sea poured into a dry, newly collapsed caldera once the eruption was over.

position.detail: Fig. 2a (PDF page 4): dotted orange line, vector drawing

features.evidence: The dotted orange line marks the location of the erosional headwall, the dashed orange line the channel sides

features.label: NW strait channel, east side
features.what: East edge of the submarine channel cut when the sea flooded the caldera.
features.result: The channel is 3 km long and 1 km wide; flooding took less than a couple of days.

position.detail: Fig. 2a (PDF page 4): dashed orange line, east side

features.evidence: The new multi-beam bathymetric data show that the NW strait consists of a 3 km long, 1 km wide, U-shaped, submarine channel with an arcuate headwall

features.label: NW strait channel, west side
features.what: West edge of the submarine channel cut when the sea flooded the caldera.
features.result: Together with the east side it shows the breach was cut after the eruption, not by the collapse.

position.detail: Fig. 2a (PDF page 4): dashed orange line, west side

features.evidence: Inflow of water and associated landsliding cut a deep, 2.0–2.5 km3, submarine channel, thus filling the caldera in less than a couple of days.

features.label: Old central island (Druitt 1992)
features.what: Lost island in the middle of the pre-eruption lagoon, as drawn in the 1992 model (also Druitt and others 1999).
features.result: Its rocks were found as lumps in the Minoan ash; the old caldera was a shallow lagoon.

position.detail: Karatson 2018 Fig. 1 inset "Druitt & Francaviglia 1992, Druitt et al. 1999": inner loop, 16.7 km2; fitted with the Thera, Therasia and Aspronisi coast as control

features.evidence: refined the likely extension of the pre-Minoan caldera, which may indeed have been restricted to the northern part of the present-day caldera
features.notes: Outline traced by us from a small schematic inset (Karatson and others 2018, Fig. 1 upper left) and fitted to today's coast by matching the grey island silhouette (overlap 0.78 to 0.80). It is a published model, not a survey. Area 16.7 km2 as traced, about 4.6 km across if round.

features.label: Old caldera lagoon (Druitt 2014)

features.result: Fits the Minoan ash, which holds stromatolites and shells from a shallow bay.

features.label: Old central island (Druitt 2014)
features.what: Lost island ("Pre-Kameni") inside the lagoon, as drawn in the 2014 model.
features.result: Lava lumps from it are in the Minoan ash.

position.detail: Karatson 2018 Fig. 1 inset "Druitt 2014": innermost loop, 8.5 km2

features.evidence: a central island referred to as ‘Pre-Kameni’ after the present-day Kameni Islands.
features.notes: Outline traced by us from a small schematic inset (Karatson and others 2018, Fig. 1 upper left) and fitted to today's coast by matching the grey island silhouette (overlap 0.78 to 0.80). It is a published model, not a survey. Area 8.5 km2 as traced, about 3.3 km across if round.

features.label: Old central island (Athanassas 2016)
features.what: Lost island in the north basin, as drawn in the 2016 model built on cosmic-ray dating of the old caldera wall.
features.result: Supports a pre-Minoan caldera, with a ring of water around an island.

position.detail: Karatson 2018 Fig. 1 inset "Athanassas et al. 2016": island loop, 9.8 km2

features.evidence: refined the likely extension of the pre-Minoan caldera, which may indeed have been restricted to the northern part of the present-day caldera
features.notes: Outline traced by us from a small schematic inset (Karatson and others 2018, Fig. 1 upper left) and fitted to today's coast by matching the grey island silhouette (overlap 0.78 to 0.80). It is a published model, not a survey. Area 9.8 km2 as traced, about 3.5 km across if round. Karatson 2018 gives its volume as 2.2 to 2.5 km3 and its growth start as 20.2 ± 1.0 ka. The outer line of this model is open to the north and was not traced.

measurements.what: Date of the eruption from radiocarbon on the olive branch (outermost ring), 95.4% range
measurements.plato_value: 9,000 years before the telling, about 9600 BCE (Timaeus 23e; Critias 108e)
measurements.evidence: we determined the calibrated age range of the outermost ring to 1621–1605 B.C. (1σ, 68% confidence) or 1627–1600 B.C. (2σ, 95% confidence)

measurements.what: Date from Bayesian analysis of radiocarbon across the Aegean (Manning and others 2006)
measurements.unit: BCE (late 17th century, as the paper words it)
measurements.evidence: show that the Santorini (Thera) eruption must have occurred in the late 17th century B.C.

measurements.what: Date from pottery and Egyptian links (archaeological dating), as summarised in 2018
measurements.evidence: a discrepancy between radiocarbon (late 17th-early 16th century BCE) and archaeological (mid 16th-early 15th century BCE) dating evidence for Thera.

measurements.what: Date from the 2023 reanalysis of the Phira olive branch, simple ordered sequence, IntCal20, 95.4%
measurements.unit: BCE (72.3% share; the other 23.2% is 1621 to 1598)
measurements.evidence: the sample died either between 1621 and 1598 BCE (23.2%) or between 1593 and 1540 BCE (72.3%)

measurements.what: Years between the eruption (about 1600 BCE) and Plato's date for the sinking (about 9600 BCE)
measurements.evidence: constrain the eruption date to the range 1627-1600 B.C. with 95.4% probability

measurements.what: Size of the flooded caldera today
measurements.plato_value: Whole city 27 stades across: 5 for the island plus rings of 1, 2, 2, 3 and 3 each side (Critias 115e-116a); about 5.0 km at 185 m a stade
measurements.evidence: The LBA caldera is 10 × 7 km wide, comprises three flat-floored basins around the Kameni edifices

measurements.what: Width of the lost central island if round, from our trace of the Druitt 2014 and Athanassas 2016 outlines
measurements.plato_value: 5 stades across, about 925 m at 185 m a stade (Critias 116a)
measurements.evidence: a 2.4 km3 Pre-Kameni island (with ideal low dome shape) in the centre of the flooded bay
constrain the volume of Pre-Kameni to 2.2–2.5 km3.

measurements.what: Volume of the eruption deposits, bulk and as solid rock (DRE)
measurements.evidence: The Minoan eruptive products may comprise up to 117–129 km3 bulk volume, corresponding to 78–86 km3 DRE

measurements.what: Volume of the eruption as given by Nomikou and others
measurements.evidence: discharging 30–80 km3 DRE (dense-rock equivalent) of silicic pyroclastic deposits

measurements.what: Height the tsunami reached on the Cretan coast at Palaikastro
measurements.plato_value: "violent earthquakes and floods"; the island sank in a day and night (Timaeus 25c-d)
measurements.evidence: Field evidence suggests that tsunami waves at Palaikastro were at least 9 m high.

measurements.what: Height above sea level of a layer read as a tsunami deposit on Santorini
measurements.evidence: a sediment layer interpreted as a tsunami deposit on Santorini 10–12 m above sea level

measurements.what: Time for the sea to refill the caldera through the north-west strait

story.line: In 1939 Marinatos tied the end of Minoan palaces to a Thera eruption. Galanopoulos and Luce later said that eruption inspired Plato's sunken island.
From 1967 Marinatos dug Akrotiri and found a real Bronze Age town under the ash. It proved the eruption but not the Plato link.
Radiocarbon on olive branches from Phira and Therasia dates the eruption to the 17th or 16th century BCE. Plato's date is about 8,000 years earlier.
On Crete, about 155 km away, Palaikastro holds a layer read as a tsunami at least 9 m high, laid down just after the first ash.
Before the eruption the caldera held a shallow lagoon with a central island. Models differ on its shape. It was blown apart; the Kameni islands grew later.
Ships mapped the strait and seismic lines show the sea broke in after the eruption and refilled the caldera in under two days.
In 2023 IODP drilled the caldera floor and the sea around it, to read the ash and flows that Santorini and Kolumbo laid down.

Both are about palace destruction layers on Crete, with no Thera positions; only the abstracts were read, and neither abstract names Atlantis in connection with Thera.
